newsitem.title: USA: Judge will not reinstate teen's lawyer in baby death.
newsitem.headline: Judge will not reinstate teen's lawyer in baby death.

text.p: The judge in the case of a New Jersey teenager charged with killing her newborn son said he would not reinstate her lawyer, who was removed for violating a gag order.

Judge Henry duPont Ridgely of the Delaware Superior Court disqualified Robert Gottlieb last week for violating a gag order against pretrial publicity by allowing the defendant, Amy Grossberg, to be interviewed by Barbara Walters on ABC's "20/20" programme.
Grossberg, along with her high school sweetheart Brian Peterson, was charged with murder last year when the body of their newborn son was found in a trash container near the University of Delaware.
Ridgely refused Tuesday to change his mind, saying he had not "misapprehended either the law or the facts."

In a court filing Monday seeking the review, Gottlieb and Grossberg included an impassioned handwritten letter by Grossberg's parents "begging" Ridgely to reconsider. They said their daughter's June 6 interview with Walters was intended only to counter negative press reports.
"Please understand that we are just ordinary people ... (whose) daughter was portrayed worldwide as a 'baby killer,' a spoiled, rich, uncaring and ungiving person," wrote Sonye and Alan Grossberg.

"Mr. Gottlieb did in no way initiate, contact, interview or even orchestrate any media including the 20/20 show. This was our opportunity finally to tell the world that our Amy is a person, our child, a loving daughter ... We intended no disrespect to the court," they said.

In a statement Tuesday, Gottlieb said "What has happened here is inherently unfair to Amy Grossberg ... No one, not Amy, her parents or any of her prior Delaware attorneys thought that the Court prohibited them from speaking to Barbara Walters ... We will appeal Judge Ridgely's original decision and his denial of our motion to reconsider."
Grossberg and Peterson are set to be tried beginning Oct. 6. If convicted, they could face the death penalty.
